messages:
sam: heads up: debugging an SDK bug when using python async client with Dedicated behind customer's proxy. sync (requests) accepts custom CA file, async (httpx) fails TLS.
jord: can you share the minimal repro and how you pass the CA? verify=path or env var?
sam: I passed verify='/etc/ssl/redwood-root.pem' into sdk.AsyncClient(verify=...) and also tried building httpx.AsyncClient(verify='...') and injecting that. Sync path works. Async -> ssl.SSLCertVerificationError unable to get local issuer.
jord: our async wrapper injects a custom transport for retries/proxy. my guess: the SSLContext creation step is skipped for str verify if our wrapper expects bool. check typing in stubs.
sam: i printed the async client's internal transport ssl context and it's None; sync client has a context.
jord: ok please open an issue. quick workaround: create SSLContext manually and pass it as verify. example: import ssl; ctx=ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/redwood-root.pem'); httpx.AsyncClient(verify=ctx) then pass into sdk.AsyncClient(httpx_client=...). that worked for me in staging.
sam: posted that snippet in the new issue. also: can we standardize env var names in docs? REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE vs SSL_CERT_FILE vs httpx behavior confused me.
ops-bot: Issue created: SDK-5112 "py async client: custom CA path ignored when building SSLContext inside wrapper" assigned jord.
jord: plan: 1) fix conditional to treat str/bytes separately from bool; 2) update type hints to Union[bool,str,ssl.SSLContext]; 3) ensure retry middleware reuses ssl context when recreating transports; 4) add a small unit that builds a local cert and asserts transport._ssl_context is present.
sam: thanks. also please add a quick note in python quickstart showing both sync and async examples for custom CA + Dedicated. saved me hours.
jord: will do in PR, ETA this week.
